crop: Zucchini / courgette (Cucurbita pepo L.), bush type, harvested immature
naming_warning: Cameroon statistics only report the FAO group 'pumpkins, squash and gourds' (mostly Cucurbita moschata/maxima and seed cucurbits), never courgette alone (S8, S1). Temple's 1998 quantification of Cameroon fruit and vegetable flows lists no courgette line at all (S13), which suggests courgette is a niche crop for urban and supermarket demand.

cycle.establishment: Direct sowing recommended; transplanting possible at the 3 to 4 leaf stage (S2, S4, S5). Germination in 5 to 7 days (S1, S2, S5).

sowing_to_first_flower_days.notes: Flowering begins 30 to 40 days after seedling emergence (S1); blooms about 45 to 55 days after planting (Kenya, S5).

observations.where: PROTA, courgette harvested at 20 to 25 cm
PROTA, first immature fruits 50 to 60 days after germination
Kenya input supplier, about 2 to 2.5 months, fruits 10 to 20 cm

total_cycle_days.notes: PROTA timings give 85 to 100 days (55 to 60 + 30 to 40, derived) (S1). FAO-56 stage lengths 20/30/25/15 = 90 and 25/35/25/15 = 100 days (Mediterranean/arid) (S9). Kenyan guides imply up to about 165 days (75 + 90, derived) (S2).

60 to 100 cm x 60 cm, 2 to 3 seeds per hill, thinned to 1 plant

seed_rate.notes: No source gives a seed rate in kg/ha. Derived seed count: 13,889 to 40,000 hills/ha x 2 to 3 seeds per hill (S1, S2, S3). Converting to kg needs a sourced 1000-seed weight, which was not found.
seed_rate.kg_per_ha_basis: Only kg figure found: about 2.25 kg of seed gives enough transplants for 1 ha of cucumbers and zucchini (British Columbia, temperate) (S26). No African direct-seeding kg/ha figure found.

seeds_per_ha_direct_seeded_derived.notes: Derived: 22,000 to 26,000 seeds per acre (S27) / 0.4047 ha per acre = 54,361 to 64,245 seeds/ha; consistent with the 27,800 to 120,000 seeds/ha derived from African spacings.

sowing_depth_cm.notes: 1.5 cm (S3); 2 cm (S2, S4); about 2.5 cm (S1). Seed soaking 3 days between wet towels, sow only partly germinated seed (S3).

trellising.practice: Not needed for bush courgette; none of the sources describes staking.

mulch.practice: Plastic mulch may give good control of soil-linked fruit rots (Pythium, Phytophthora) if water drains freely off the mulch (S1). Avoid fruit and vines lying on wet soil (wet rot) (S4).

itinerary.description: Prepare land 2 to 3 months before planting (Kenya, S5). Pre-plant herbicide example from a Kenyan input supplier: Clampdown 480SL 200 ml per 20 L (active ingredient not stated) (S2). In Centre Cameroon cucurbits are commonly sown after slash and burn of fallow (S12); no quantified data on burning effects for courgette was found.

inputs.product: Clampdown 480SL (pre-plant herbicide; a.i. not stated in source)

itinerary.description: Raised beds about 25 cm high (S3) or mounds about 10 inches high and up to 2 ft in diameter about 4 ft apart (S5); double rows on 1.2 m beds for bush types (S1). Good drainage matters: heavy rain above 40 mm in one day causes waterlogging and stem splitting (S1).

Organic matter 50 to 70 t/ha in the planting hole or furrow (S1); one wheelbarrow of compost and/or manure per square metre (S3). Mineral: PROTA recommends 150 kg N, 150 kg P, 300 kg K per ha, half before planting (S1). Kenya: DAP 50 kg per acre before sowing, about 1 teaspoon per hole, mixed well with soil (S2, S4), i.e. about 124 kg/ha (derived); Humipower 1 kg per 50 kg DAP and/or 1 t manure (S2).

inputs.product: Mineral NPK to supply half of 150 N / 150 P / 300 K
inputs.unit: 75 N + 75 P + 150 K kg/ha (product not specified)

itinerary.description: Direct sow 2 to 3 seeds per hill, 1.5 to 2.5 cm deep (S1, S2, S3). F1 hybrids preferred; they yield 50 to 100% more than open-pollinated cultivars (S1). Varieties named in Kenya: Ambassador F1, Simba F1, Black Beauty, Cera F1, Green Zucchini (S2, S4, S5). Seed soak option: Optimizer 20 ml/L (S2).

inputs.unit: kg/ha not sourced; 27,800 to 120,000 seeds/ha derived

itinerary.description: Thin to one plant per hill after emergence (S2, S4) or keep the strongest plant after 2 to 3 weeks (S3).

CAN 50 to 100 kg per acre (about 124 to 247 kg/ha, derived) 3 to 4 weeks after sowing, placed about 15 cm from the plant; urea as alternative (S2). PROTA: second half of mineral fertilizer 30 days after planting (S1). Compost top dressing at 4 weeks plus weekly liquid fertilizer 1 L in 10 L water at the root zone (S3).

inputs.unit: kg/ha (range 124 to 247, derived from 50 to 100 kg/acre)

inputs.product: Mineral NPK, second half of 150 N / 150 P / 300 K

itinerary.description: Kenyan input-supplier programme (trade names, compositions not stated): 1 week after germination Lavender Super Starter 20 ml/20 L or Goldchance Super Start 50 g/20 L; vegetative Goldchance Super Growth 50 g/20 L or Lavender Super Vegetative 20 ml/20 L; flowering and fruiting Goldchance Super Flowers and Fruits 50 g/20 L, Dimiphite 20 ml/20 L, Goldchance Multisuper K 50 g/20 L; sticker Integra 3 ml/20 L (S2). Generic foliar 0.5 L in 20 L water (S3). No efficacy data.

itinerary.description: About 2.5 cm (25 mm) of water per week (S1). Optimum supply 800 mm during vegetative growth, irrigation in dry areas (S4, S2). Keep soil moderately moist, more water at flowering and fruiting (S2). FAO-56: Kc ini 0.5 (cucurbit group value), Kc mid 0.95, Kc end 0.75 (S9).

irrigation_l_per_plant_per_day.notes: Not found. At 25 mm/week and 14,000 to 40,000 plants/ha this would be about 0.9 to 2.6 L/plant/day (derived: 250,000 L per ha per week / 7 / plants).

itinerary.description: No courgette-specific weeding schedule found. Weed control reduces Zeugodacus cucurbitae infestation on cucurbits in Cote d'Ivoire (S6).

Main threats: powdery mildew (main leaf disease), fruit flies (serious losses in West Africa), aphids, whitefly, Epilachna beetles, pickleworm and melon worm, spider mites above 30 C, fruit rots from soil splash, PRSV-W virus (S1). Kenyan supplier rates per 20 L (active ingredients not stated): fruit flies Presento 200SP 5 g, Kingcode Elite 50EC 10 ml or Profile 440EC 30 ml; aphids Kingcode Elite 10 ml, Lexus 247SC 8 ml, Pentagon 50EC 10 ml; mites Alonze 50EC 5 ml; whitefly Taurus 500SP 10 g; thrips Defender 25EC 40 ml; downy mildew Fortress Gold 720WP 40 g, Tower 720WP 50 g, Katerina 720SC 40 ml; powdery mildew Ransom 600WP 15 g, Domain 250EC 10 ml, Absolute 375SC 10 ml; anthracnose Ducasse 250EW 20 ml; preventive Cadilac 800WP 50 g; damping off Pyramid 700WP 100 g drench (S2). Avermectin-treated cucurbit plots had lower fruit fly infestation in Cote d'Ivoire; remove infested fruits; insect-proof netting (S6). Production timed for the early dry season because aphid pressure is lower (S1).

itinerary.description: Pollination by insects, mainly bees and wasps; placing bee hives in the field during flowering often improves pollination and yield (S1). Under cool conditions (nights 10 C, days 20 C) parthenocarpic fruit set may occur (S1). Hive density not given.

Harvest courgettes at 20 to 25 cm (S1), 10 to 20 cm (S2, S4) or about 10 cm depending on variety (S5); cut rather than pull (S3). Visit daily because fruits enlarge very quickly (S1); about three picks a week or daily (S2, S4). Bush cultivars set 5 to 8 fruits per plant (S1).

itinerary.description: Immature fruits cannot be kept beyond 5 to 6 days at 25 to 35 C; optimum storage 10 C, storage life 20 to 25 days (S1). Sell within days or cool.

pests_diseases.name: Fruit flies (Dacus ciliatus, Zeugodacus/Bactrocera cucurbitae, Dacus bivittatus)
pests_diseases.importance: Major. PROTA: Dacus cucurbitae causes serious losses in West Africa (S1). Cote d'Ivoire 2023: pupae from 72% of sampled zucchinis; zucchini produced more pupae per fruit than cucumber; D. ciliatus more frequent on zucchini (S6). Cameroon (Yaounde, Koutaba in Noun): 36.7 to 37.1% cucurbit fruit losses, D. bivittatus and D. ciliatus major; zucchini not sampled, C. moschata among most affected (S7).
pests_diseases.controls: Sanitation, weed control, insect-proof netting, avermectin (S6); Kenyan products in itinerary (S2).

pests_diseases.name: Aphids (Aphis gossypii)
pests_diseases.importance: Direct damage and virus vector; lower pressure in early dry season (S1).

pests_diseases.name: Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci B / B. argentifolia)
pests_diseases.controls: Taurus 500SP 10 g/20 L, Lexus 247SC 8 ml/20 L (S2).

pests_diseases.name: Epilachna and other cucurbit beetles
pests_diseases.importance: Direct damage; vectors of squash mosaic virus (S1).
pests_diseases.controls: Kingcode Elite 50EC 10 ml/20 L, Sinophate 750SP 20 g/20 L (S2).

pests_diseases.name: Pickleworm (Diaphania nitidalis) and melon worm (Diaphania hyalinata)
Spider mites (Tetranychus spp.)
pests_diseases.importance: Attack leaves when day temperatures exceed 30 C (S1).
pests_diseases.controls: Alonze 50EC 5 ml/20 L, Bazooka 18EC 10 ml/20 L (S2).

pests_diseases.name: Powdery mildew (Erysiphe cichoracearum; Sphaerotheca fuliginea in drier conditions)
pests_diseases.importance: Main leaf disease; resistant hybrids exist (S1).

pests_diseases.name: Downy mildew (Pseudoperonospora cubensis)
pests_diseases.importance: Usually minor localized lesions on this crop (S1); promoted by humidity and heavy rain (S3, S4).
pests_diseases.controls: Fortress Gold, Tower, Katerina, Gearlock Turbo (S2).

pests_diseases.name: Anthracnose (Colletotrichum lagenarium) and scab (Cladosporium cucumerinum)
pests_diseases.importance: More likely at higher elevations because lowland temperatures exceed their optimum (S1): relevant to Foumbot at 1,000 to 1,200 m.

pests_diseases.name: Wet rot (Choanephora cucurbitarum), Pythium and Phytophthora fruit/root rots, Rhizoctonia, Sclerotium rolfsii, Fusarium solani
pests_diseases.importance: Blossom-end and soil-contact rots, rain splash (S1); wet rot when vines lie on the ground (S4).

pests_diseases.name: Viruses: PRSV-W (main in lowland tropics), squash mosaic virus (seed-borne), CMV, WMV2, ZYMV (rare in tropics)
pests_diseases.importance: Listed (S1); mosaic virus listed in Kenya (S2, S4).

optimal_day_temp_c.notes: Best growth days 24 to 29 C, nights 16 to 24 C; tolerates monthly mean day temperatures of 18 to 28 C (S1). Kenyan sources print an optimum of 15 to 22 C (S2, S4, S5), which conflicts with PROTA.

heat_stress_threshold_c.notes: Not a physiological threshold: spider mites invade leaves above 30 C day temperature (S1). C. pepo is less heat resistant than C. moschata (S1).

climate.rain_humidity_sensitivity: Heavy rain above 40 mm per day causes waterlogging and stem splitting in bush cultivars (S1); heavy rains destroy flowers and promote mildew, plant in full sun (S3, S4); crop less suited to the rainy season, production mostly at the start of the dry season (S1); Z. cucurbitae infestation higher in the rainy season May to July in Cote d'Ivoire (S6).

planting_windows_foumbot.proposal: Best: sow late September to November so the crop flowers and is harvested in the early dry season (mid November to February), with irrigation. Possible: sow at the onset of rains (mid March to April) so harvest ends before the heaviest rains, accepting higher mildew and fruit-fly risk. Avoid sowing that puts flowering in the peak rainy months.
planting_windows_foumbot.basis: Analyst inference from PROTA (early dry season production, rain damage thresholds) and Kenyan guides (avoid heavy rains); not a sourced Foumbot recommendation.

confidence_notes: OVERALL: medium for agronomy (mostly PROTA plus Kenyan extension-style articles), very low for economics. (1) No Cameroon-specific agronomic, yield, price, cost or margin data for courgette was found; courgette does not appear in Cameroon vegetable flow statistics (S13), consistent with a niche urban/supermarket crop. (2) Prices, cost of production, margins and labour are all null: these are the biggest gaps and require primary data collection in Foumbot, Bafoussam, Douala and Yaounde (supermarkets, hotel and restaurant buyers). (3) Temperature optimum conflicts: PROTA 24 to 29 C day vs Kenyan articles 15 to 22 C. (4) PROTA fertilizer 150-150-300 may be elemental or oxide; Kenyan programme supplies no potassium. (5) Seed rate in kg/ha could not be sourced. (6) Varieties named in the brief (Clarita, Diamant F1, Black Beauty in West Africa) were not found in African sources reached except Black Beauty in Kenya. (7) Research was cut short when the shared web search quota ran out; Infonet-Biovision, Martinique Chamber of Agriculture courgette sheet and FAOSTAT API were blocked. Seed company guides (Technisem, Tropicasem) and ANADER/ISRA courgette sheets remain to be checked. FOLLOW-UP ROUND (Oct 2026): added a Cote d'Ivoire per-kg price series 2024 to 2026 (CNLVC and Sika Finance), a low-reliability Cameroon retail estimate (535 to 714 XAF/kg, Selina Wamucii) with a derived wholesale of about 375 to 500 XAF/kg, Kenya HCDA 2011-13 implied prices (KES 24.5 to 38.9/kg) and yields (9.2 to 10.4 t/ha), Kenyan seed pack prices, and a temperate seed quantity of 2.25 kg/ha (transplants).
